title: Example: the gamut window
lead: An example of InkProf’s ICC-derived colour volume in a separate window.
images: Figure 6. InkProf’s gamut view using an example sRGB profile (ICC v2). sRGB illustrates the window; this is not a measured printer gamut.
sections: Read the axes and surface

L* represents lightness. a* runs from green to red, b* from blue to yellow. The surface is calculated from the profile’s colour transform in CIELAB D50. Rotate the view in the app; the PDF image is static.
Use the view as supporting information

A larger surface is not itself a quality score. Assess measurements, colour errors and real prints. In a printer project, Select area chooses regions for manual reinforcement with additional measured samples. See page 56.

title: Two stages of smoothing
sections: Before profile building: Measurement data smoothing

B2 offers Argyll only (raw measurements), without separate pre-smoothing, and Argyll colprof pre-smoothing (experimental), with an intermediate model. Original spectra, XYZ and raw readings are retained. Distinguish this B2 choice from Row 15: Argyll only, which selects additional patches.
Argyll: Assumed noise (%)
The first colprof model uses an assumed average deviation through -r, normally 0.5%. This is not an exact measured Delta E00. The model is evaluated at the original RGB values.
At ICC building: Smoothing at ICC build
This controls final colprof -r. Empty uses 0.5%. The value is independent of the first-stage noise assumption. Percentages display one decimal without rounding stored precision.
FWA/OBA and B1

B2 recipes support native M0 FWA before Argyll pre-smoothing and final fitting. Compensation is applied once, not again to derived XYZ. Changing FWA preserves B1 but requires new B2 and later results. See the M0 white-reference section.

title: Test RGB gradients
sections: B2 selection and Manual B3

With pre-regularization selected, tick Open RGB gradient test after profile build. The window opens after successful Manual B3. Save recipe in B2 does not start the check. Automatic B3 creates its own recipes and does not use this B2 choice.
Run RGB check

Nine RGB paths with 1,025 samples each are evaluated through the final ICC. Select a path and relative or perceptual intent. Curves show RGB, Lab, adjacent Delta E00 steps and Lab second differences. JSON and Markdown are saved in the job's checks folder.
Check blue-sky inverse
The blue-sky test uses B2A and returns through A2B. It complements the forward check and changes neither recipe nor ICC. Reopen a closed window with inkprof.checkRGBGradients(jobFolder).
Interpretation

Large local steps, reversals and second differences identify places to investigate. Real printer curvature can also produce these values. No universal pass threshold is used. Printed gradients and documented viewing conditions are needed for physical assessment.

title: Remeasure a whole printed row
sections: New measurement or earlier revision

Measure starts a new measurement. Saved revisions selects an earlier saved revision. Import file reads an external file. For isolated problems, use Remeasure patch or Remeasure row in the overview. A new save preserves previous history.
Select page and row

Remeasure row uses the printed page and row number. B24 means position B, row 24; patch ID is separate. Original scan mode, tolerance and instrument conditions are retained. An isolated session measures only the selected row.
Measure and review

Click Measure selected row, calibrate and follow FORWARD/REVERSE. Save supplies candidate values. Change Delta E00 compares previous and new measurements, not error against desired colour. Accept row replacement creates a revision replacing only this row. Discard / Close retains previous values.
Preserved traceability

Original data, new raw readings and the decision are saved. Old paired readings are labelled historical after row replacement. Select and review the correct workflow revision before locking B1 again; Accept in the remeasurement window does not necessarily select profiling input.

title: C2: profile, TIFF and print chain
sections: Conversion and tag

Lab-based targets use B2A, absolute colorimetry and BPC off. Layout and RGB16 quantization follow. The exact printer ICC is now embedded as a tag without another pixel conversion. Earlier exports do not change when code is updated.
Keep already converted values

When opening in Photoshop, discard/ignore the embedded profile without converting RGB values; do not convert to a working space. Print at 100% without further colour conversion. Assigned sRGB or Adobe RGB followed by conversion can greatly change older untagged targets. Read PRINTING.txt and document the chain.
Contents and difficult colours

The profiling-workflow default is 80 colours, 24 neutrals, 12 challenges and 12 repeats. Counts can be changed. Challenges may be outside gamut or have an unresolved inverse. C2 therefore does not contain only previous problem colours.
White margin

An unprinted margin uses pure device RGB white. A white image area converted with absolute intent may receive colour to reproduce the reference white point. This is not the paper's own whiteness. A converted image margin and the target background are therefore different things.

title: Read the C3 table and warnings
sections: Identity and Lab

Page and Coordinate identify position. ID is identity and Role is patch type. Desired Lab is desired colour; Measured Lab is the print. L* is lightness, negative/positive a* green/red and negative/positive b* blue/yellow.
Two error columns

Measured vs desired (dE00) compares measurement with desired colour. Model vs measurement (dE00) compares ICC prediction with measurement. Similar numbers do not mean similar colours: if both are large, measurement differs from both. Near zero in the second column means close model agreement.
Sorting and groups

Largest errors appear first. Main statistics include unique patches, including challenges, but not extra repeats. Filter groups before drawing conclusions. Small differences between repeats or forward/reverse show repeatability, not accuracy.
Suspected double colour management

C3 simulates extra conversion from sRGB and Adobe RGB to the printer profile and warns when a simulation explains measurements much better. This is a hypothesis; other print faults may look similar. Check assignment, conversion and the driver before retraining the model.

title: Reference colours and an existing ICC
sections: Fixed reference set

C2 can use a Lab table, Argyll CIE/CGATS with Lab or XYZ, or TI1 with device RGB. Use only material you are entitled to use. Names and patch codes are preserved for C3. A reference name does not imply protected vendor layout or data are included.
Lab or RGB

Lab references are converted through the ICC and test inverse, print and measurement together. Device RGB is printed as given without ICC conversion; reference Lab is the A2B prediction. PRINTING.txt and verification.json identify the method.
New project: Verify existing ICC

The separate seven-step workflow imports RGB printer profiles in ICC v2 and v4, creates a target, measures, analyses, reviews, records assessment and saves a certificate. The original colour tables are used and delivered. V4.4 is checked natively through LittleCMS; verification does not use a v2 reconstruction. The 575-patch suggestion covers skin tones, shadows, neutrals and broad colours.
Unknown independence

If original training data are unavailable, independence is unknown. Numerical checks and a good photographic impression do not give automatic approval or ISO certification. Document intended use, the chain and limitations.
Methods in RGB Target

The RGB target designer offers OFPS, incremental far point, quasi-random, body-centred cubic and random through Argyll. An existing ICC can guide patch placement but is not measurement data. Argyll preconditioning with v4 needs a separate, explicitly accepted approximate v2 copy; the original is preserved.

title: Diagnose with JSON and the right check
sections: Traceable chain

B1 locks measurement input. The job saves recipe.json, status.json and result/profile.icc. C2 saves an exact ICC copy, desired Lab, RGB16 and placement in verification.json. C3 links measurement JSON and its TI3 revision through hashes. Coordinate and ID are different identifiers.
Built-in MATLAB checks

inkprof.checkProfileFit checks the forward model against training. inkprof.checkProfileGrid and inkprof.checkProfileC1 provide grid, CMM and inverse diagnostics. inkprof.checkVerificationTarget compares the verification print. inkprof.checkRGBGradients opens the gradient window. Read each check's purpose.
Separate scripts are not app buttons

The development measurement-JSON inverse script compared Lab, inverse RGB and return through A2B. It is not a built-in InkProf function. Small Lab-RGB-Lab error shows internal consistency, not a correct physical print. Alternative solutions can give large RGB differences.
Test the hypothesis first

First check suspected wrong ICC or inverse numerically and through hashes, without another print. Check a suspected wrong row against TI2 and by remeasurement. A changed print chain may require a new sample with identical device RGB. Do not rebuild the model to conceal an unresolved chain error.

title: Compare accuracy and gradients
sections: Open the comparison

After valid B1, choose Compare accuracy and gradients in the main window. Enter one to six positive final colprof -r values. Compare the currently offered Argyll candidates.  Several builds may take minutes; progress is displayed.
Read the results

Argyll mode builds one -r 1.0 candidate. InkProf mode compares -r 0.5, 1.0 and 1.5 at high quality when development controls exist. Selection balances development error against float-gradient smoothness and guards against regressions. The default permits at most 0.05 ΔE00 worsening in weighted RMS error for at least 5% gradient improvement. In InkProf mode without development controls it builds one engine-default candidate. These numerical rules are not print acceptance criteria.
Automatic B3 selection

With development controls, Automatic tests final -r values 0.5, 1 and 1.5 at high table quality. Selection balances accuracy and float-gradient smoothness. Guards check patch and gray regressions, curvature, reversals, coverage and colour span. Defaults permit 0.05 RMS accuracy tradeoff for at least 5% gradient improvement. These are numerical selection rules, not print acceptance criteria. Without development controls, one candidate is built with no claim of superiority.
Choose deliberately

Comparison preserves B1 and leaves the current workflow ICC selected. To use a comparison setting, enter it in B2 and build Manual B3. New recipes support FWA before pre-smoothing with the measured-white requirements described in the M0 section.

title: Photographic gradient conversion
sections: Open the diagnostic

Choose Photographic gradients in the main window after a successful profile build, or in the RGB gradient window. The check uses the exact selected ICC and saves JSON and Markdown in its checks folder.
What is tested

Nine paths with 1,025 samples are converted from sRGB and Adobe RGB (1998) to printer RGB, then through relative A2B to predicted Lab. Relative and perceptual intent, BPC on/off, and float, 16-bit and 8-bit input/output buffers give 216 combinations. LittleCMS performs these conversions; Photoshop and printer drivers may behave differently.The count is 9 paths × 2 source spaces × 2 intents × 2 BPC settings × 3 precisions = 216; input and output use the same precision.
Read the columns

Curvature P95 measures normalized Lab second differences. L* reversals count decreasing lightness steps on eligible interior points; interpret them in relation to the chosen path. Unique RGB codes and unchanged steps describe quantization plateaus. The JSON also records longest plateau and Lab span. Large numbers are not automatically visible defects.
Limits of the test

Hard device clipping is excluded from comparison metrics, but this is not a proven physical-gamut mask. Quantization plateaus are expected, especially at 8 bit. Compare matching paths and precision. Numerical smoothness does not certify absence of banding; verify printed gradients.

title: Certificate evidence
sections: Pre-regularization in the certificate

The certificate records the selected job recipe, pre-regularization method, its assumed noise (avgdev) and final colprof -r. Saved results include the model change when available. Raw measurements are preserved. Model change is not print accuracy.
Gradient evidence and regeneration

A saved photographic-gradient report is included only if its SHA-256 matches the certificate ICC. The certificate summarizes CMM, settings, sample count, interior coverage, reversals and curvature, and embeds full per-path evidence in JSON. Missing evidence is stated explicitly. Re-run step 14 for a new certificate; historical and signed certificates are preserved.

title: ICC rendering intents
sections: B2 and rendering intents

Newly built profiles support perceptual, relative colorimetric and absolute colorimetric in one ICC file. B2 provides Perceptual compression (%), passed to colprof -s. The default 20% generic compression is a starting setting, not a measured optimum. Automatic B3 carries forward this B2 value.
What the ICC contains

Perceptual uses a gamut-mapped B2A0 table. Relative uses B2A1. Absolute uses the relative table plus the media white point (wtpt); it does not require a separate B2A3 table. The colour-management application selects the rendering intent. The profile header default does not prevent choosing another intent.Saturation is the fourth ICC intent and uses saturation tables when available. This discussion focuses on the three photographic intents; the version choice on page 46 also concerns saturation.
Build validation and certificate

New builds require perceptual and relative tables with distinct data and a valid media-white tag before publication. Saved jobs and certificates record the rendering-intent settings. Structural validation and numerical conversions do not establish print quality.
Update an existing profile

Build a changed profile with a new B2 recipe and Manual B3. Existing profiles and measurements are retained. Check numerical results and verify the new profile in a fresh print before approval. C2 still uses absolute colorimetry without BPC; print RGB unchanged without further conversion.

title: ICC v2 or v4.4: which fits best?
lead: Choose according to the printing application, rendering intent and checked results. A higher version number does not itself make a profile more colour-accurate.
sections: What v4 adds
ICC v4 clarifies the reference colour space and rendering intents for more predictable interpretation across profiles and engines. It does not replace good measurements or print assessment.
When v2 is a good choice
Keep v2 in a working, checked workflow, particularly for older applications or recipients requiring it. InkProf uses v2 internally for Argyll. Do not switch solely for a higher version number.
When v4.4 is a good choice

Choose v4.4 when the application and recipient support it and the result has been assessed. InkProf preserves colorimetric tables but remaps perceptual and saturation tables. Shadows and transitions may change; improvement is not guaranteed.
Both for comparison

Both gives both versions from the same profiling run. Compare the same photograph, gradients and shadows with the same paper, ink, settings, intent and viewing light. Record BPC and change one part of the chain at a time.
Numerical BPC example

Two profiles were tested through LittleCMS at sRGB greys 0, 8, 32, 128 and 255. Perceptual v4.4 gave identical results with BPC on and off; predicted L* differed by at most 0.79 from v2 with BPC on. This is a numerical example, not a new print measurement or general guarantee.
What verification establishes

C2 uses absolute colorimetry without BPC. A good result does not establish your preferred perceptual rendering. The certificate identifies the checked profile and v4.4 conversion separately. Also assess a print using the production version and intent.
Import and the practical decision

InkProf imports RGB printer profiles in v2 and v4. Existing v4 verification uses the original through LittleCMS. Argyll preconditioning requires an accepted approximate v2 copy. Choose according to your chain, measurements and image assessment.
links: ICC: reasons for changing to v4

title: TIFF: conversion versus embedded ICC
sections: Read the companion text file

PRINTING.txt beside modern TIFF targets, and *-README.txt for the legacy exporter, list ICC conversion and Embedded ICC separately. Tagged files identify the printer profile and its SHA-256. C2 also has package-level PRINTING.txt; read it together with print/PRINTING.txt.
Conversion: what changed the pixels?

Base and refinement targets render source device RGB directly without a printer ICC conversion by InkProf. Ordinary C2 colour-reference targets have already passed through the printer ICC once, absolute colorimetric without BPC. C2 device-RGB reference sets instead print their RGB unchanged; the ICC predicts reference Lab only. Imported source history may be unknown.
Tag: what identifies the file?

Both kinds of C2 TIFF embed the printer ICC as an identifying tag. Embedding alone changes no pixels and is not an instruction to apply the ICC again. A tag does not prove that no other conversion occurred earlier. InkProf records its own processing separately. Base and refinement targets normally have no embedded profile.
Print without another conversion

Print at 100% with colour management disabled in the application, OS print path and driver. Preserve any embedded tag without conversion. Do not assign another profile or convert the TIFF to a working space. A program can use the embedded tag if colour management is enabled. New packages contain the clearer instructions; existing TIFFs and packages are preserved.

title: Appendix: workflow diagram
lead: Overview of the example on the following pages: from planning to measured final verification and saved delivery.
sections: Using the feedback loop

When results deviate, first review measurements, profile identity and print settings. Refine only when supported by evidence; otherwise investigate or withhold approval. A new ICC requires fresh final verification. The diagram shows the print-verified route, not the separate numerical delivery route.

title: Appendix: plan and create the base target
sections: 1. Define success before printing

Agree on photographic use or a specific reference condition, viewing light, important colours and gradients, and acceptance criteria. Record printer, ink, paper, driver preset, quality, resolution, backing and instrument. Check nozzles and allow consistent drying time. A custom RGB target does not establish ISO proofing conformity.
2. Use an existing ICC as a starting estimate

Choose a reliable RGB printer ICC for the same printer, ink, paper and settings, or a reasonably similar system. In target generation, select an Argyll method supporting perceptual placement and supply the preconditioning profile. Argyll uses its predictions to distribute device-RGB patches; the base target is not converted through that ICC. A poor or unrelated profile can bias sampling. Without a suitable ICC, use an unconditioned initial target and improve the sampling after the first build.
3. Choose the measurement budget

For careful profiling, plan about 1,500-2,000 patches when time permits. About 800-1,000 is a lower-budget start. A 300-600 pilot checks setup. The design-window initial value of 575 is a smaller starting budget, not a general quality recommendation. The total includes controls and repeats. Inspect the actual count in preview. This is practical guidance, not a universal optimum.
Decision before saving

Preserve patch size and instrument scan geometry. Choose paper dimensions and inspect the actual page preview. Save the TIFF16 together with its matching TI2, layout and PRINTING.txt. Keep the original ICC and its identity with the project. A target-generation preconditioner is distinct from the profile later built from the measurements.

title: Appendix: print, measure and decide on OBA
sections: 4. Print the prepared RGB target

Follow PRINTING.txt. For a missing-profile warning in Photoshop choose Leave as is (don’t color manage). For an embedded profile that must be ignored choose Discard the embedded profile (don’t color manage). Disable further conversion and driver colour adjustment; print at 100%. Do not convert the target to Adobe RGB or apply the printer ICC again. Prepared C2 RGB must also reach the printer unchanged.
5. Measure and review before B1

Calibrate the instrument, use consistent backing and scan direction, and measure all pages. Save each measurement round as a revision. Review identities, white controls, duplicate colours and unusual readings; remeasure suspect patches or a whole row with the correct page and forward/reverse choice. Correct acquisition errors before smoothing. Select and accept the intended revision, then lock B1. Keep different print rounds identifiable.
6. Decide whether FWA/OBA compensation is needed

Do not enable compensation solely because paper looks cool or bluish or a UV lamp makes the paper glow. Consider the paper, verified measurement condition and intended viewing light. For the supported i1Pro2 M0 route, compensation is a D50 simulation using available visible spectra, not a measurement of UV excitation or an M1 result. If the paper has little OBA, or the available evidence does not support compensation, retain the uncompensated route and document the choice.
If compensation is selected

Use native M0 spectra with verified instrument metadata and sufficient spectral coverage. InkProf averages available white-patch spectra and records their count and variation. If no usable white reference exists, B2 offers blank-paper measurement, a saved approved reference, or Cancel. Measure several clean locations on the same paper with the same backing. Averaging can reduce random noise; it cannot recover missing excitation information. Save a new B2 recipe. Keep compensation and viewing assumptions consistent through comparisons and final verification; changing this choice invalidates later results.

title: Appendix: build, refine and stop
sections: 7. Choose smoothing and the B3 route

Start with Argyll only (raw measurements) when repeatability is good. If noisy measurements or gradients justify it, compare Argyll colprof pre-smoothing (experimental) against the raw route. Its Assumed noise (%) and Smoothing at ICC build are separate settings; 0.5% is the initial recipe value, not an established optimum for every instrument. Check colour fit and equivalent photographic gradient paths. Select the RGB gradient test when useful. For an exact saved B2 recipe, choose Manual in B3; Automatic creates its own recipes and does not inherit every B2 smoothing setting. With FWA and pre-smoothing, use the newly saved supported two-pass recipe.
8. Select the refinement method

Use Argyll only as the initial refinement choice: Argyll places additional patches using the current profile. Current InkProf (Jacobian sampling) uses measured local residuals and local response to propose additional RGB samples. Both routes build the resulting ICC with Argyll. Choose Jacobian sampling when a reproducible local discrepancy warrants targeted investigation; do not expect it to make unattainable colours printable. Save the choice with the proposal. Print and measure the added device-RGB target unchanged, then build the next iteration.
9. Compare equivalent evidence

Use row 18 for Previous profile prediction vs current profile prediction at common samples. Separately review fitting error, development/held-out evidence where available, repeatability, gradients and Measured print vs desired colour. A smaller training error alone is insufficient. A small inverse round-trip error only shows consistency of the model and inverse. Large measured discrepancies require checks of profile identity, RGB values, print management, patch mapping and measurement conditions before attributing them to gamut.The C3 table uses Measured vs desired (dE00) and Model vs measurement (dE00). The certificate uses Measured print vs desired colour. Profile comparison uses Previous profile prediction vs current profile prediction; this compares calculations, not a new print.
10. Decide whether another iteration is worthwhile

Continue when a specific measured uncertainty can be reduced. Stop when comparable errors and gradients show no useful improvement beyond repeatability, or a further round produces an unacceptable accuracy/smoothness trade-off. One or two comparable rounds without meaningful gain are a practical review trigger, not an automatic InkProf acceptance rule. Record the evidence, selected profile and reason for stopping. Numerical convergence does not prove physical colour accuracy or compliance.

title: Appendix: final verification and certificate
sections: 11. Verify the exact profile to be delivered

After choosing the final iteration, run row 8 (Fit, Grid and C1) and row 9 (C2: save verification TIFF16) for that current profile. Make a new control print with the documented settings and no further colour conversion. Measure it in row 10, retain the revision, and run row 11 (C3) and row 12 (feedback). Do this even if development or training measurements already look good. A measurement used to train a later build cannot independently verify that later ICC.
12. Assess the whole result

Review count, mean, median, P95 and maximum for all assessed unique colours, not only the worst patches. Identify challenge colours, controls and repeatability. Compare desired-colour error with current-profile prediction error where available. Inspect important photographs and gradients. Model-reachable, outside-model/inversion-unresolved and unclassified references describe model evidence; they are not proof of a physical gamut limit. Confirm white, black, neutral balance and the intended viewing conditions.
13. Approve or decline the intended use

In row 13, enter review notes, scope, print settings, limitations and the decision. Approval is justified only by the relevant measured evidence and agreed criteria. If a required standard limit is not met, report it; printer limitations do not waive that requirement. Photographic use may be approved with explicit limitations when agreed, while conformity for a different use is declined. If the remaining cause is unresolved, say so. Row 14 exports the selected ICC and English measurement certificate.
14. Preserve the evidence and status

Check that the certificate identifies this ICC, iteration, current verification revision, regularisation, FWA reference and reviewer decision. Retain the target, TI2/layout, PRINTING.txt, raw measurements, recipe, ICC and complete reports. Row 19 is numerical-only delivery and cannot replace fresh measured verification. If the ICC or print setup changes after approval, repeat final verification. The defensible conclusion is measured and approved for the stated use, with disclosed limits—not automatic ISO approval.

title: Appendix: evidence behind the recommendations
sections: Argyll: sampling and measurement quality

The targen documentation supports using a prior or similar ICC to guide perceptual patch placement. printtarg explains instrument-dependent patch geometry and randomised locations, which help identification and distribute spatial printing effects. Preserve the generated layout; do not rearrange patches manually. There is no universally optimal patch count. The suggested budgets in this appendix are InkProf working recommendations to be evaluated against repeatability and independent results.
Argyll: smoothing is an uncertainty assumption

colprof defines -r as the assumed average deviation of device and instrument readings, with a default of 0.5%. Raising it gives less weight to individual readings and more to collective behaviour. A percentage is not ΔE00. Estimate the need from repeat readings and compare accuracy and gradients; do not increase smoothing simply to conceal a systematic print error.
X-Rite: distinguish M0 compensation from M1

X-Rite describes M1 as the preferred condition for OBA-enhanced substrates and explains that M0 does not fully define UV content. The i1Pro2 hardware supports M1, but the InkProf path described here uses verified M0 data. Recording spectral bands near or below 400 nm does not measure the illumination spectrum or establish calibrated UV excitation. Averaging white readings improves repeatability, not the physical definition of M0. Use actual M1 measurements in a compatible workflow when required by the reference or conformity claim.
Fogra: verification needs the relevant reference and control

Fogra links contract-proof verification to its defined MediaWedge, printing condition and applicable tolerances. An InkProf custom RGB verification and reviewer approval are useful evidence for a stated use, but do not substitute for that complete procedure. The independent final control print in this appendix is an InkProf quality-control recommendation.
What external sources do not establish

These sources do not demonstrate that InkProf Jacobian sampling outperforms Argyll only, nor that the recommended patch budgets or stopping triggers are universally optimal. Those decisions require comparable local results. Sources reviewed on 8 October 2026; the handbook describes current InkProf behaviour separately from external guidance.
links: X-Rite: measurement conditions and optical brighteners

title: Appendix: comparing profiling methods
sections: A photographic starting point

Anders Torger recommends preconditioning, optimised placement and extra greys. His Colormunki example favours about 840 patches as a practical balance; this is experience with that instrument and print system, not a universal limit. He uses colprof -r1.0 to trade a little fit accuracy for smoothness and evaluates diagnostic gradients and a familiar photograph. His reported profile-matching errors compare predictions with measured device patches, including training-data checks; they are not interchangeable with InkProf C3 errors against desired colours on a separate profile-converted print. His tutorial is primarily a base-profiling workflow, not evidence that InkProf refinement replicates a particular iterative algorithm.
A more extensive measurement workflow

X-Rite’s recommended RGB workflow proposes 2,033 or 1,586 patches, wider patches for better sampling, about an hour of drying, instrument calibration and saved measurement data. These recommendations concern its own software and layouts: do not blindly increase InkProf patch width or assume one hour guarantees stability for every paper. i1Profiler also offers targeted optimisation and optical-brightener compensation; the internal engine is not Argyll, and its OBC must not be described as identical to InkProf’s M0 method.
Reconciled recommendation for InkProf

For careful profiling, plan about 1,500-2,000 patches when time permits. About 800-1,000 is a lower-budget start. A 300-600 pilot checks setup. The design-window initial value of 575 is a smaller starting budget, not a general quality recommendation. The total includes controls and repeats. Inspect the actual count in preview. This is practical guidance, not a universal optimum. Use a suitable starting ICC, neutral/white controls and reliable geometry. Select later refinement from measured evidence.
The final decision remains measured

Neither an attractive photograph nor low model-fit error alone establishes measured accuracy for the intended reference. Keep the familiar photographic check and gradient review, then make the independent final C2 print and C3 measurement before reviewer approval and certificate delivery. This combines practical photographic assessment with traceable measurement.

title: Test images
sections: Photographic test images

Keith Cooper (Northlight Images) provides printer test images and assessment notes, including the Datacolor image made available courtesy of Datacolor. Use it for overall photographic assessment of skin tones, neutrals, shadows and saturated colours. In InkProf comparisons, inspect the sky gradient for banding or uneven transitions when assessing smoothing; it is a visual diagnostic, not proof of a particular cause. Compare the same source, ICC path, intent, BPC, print preset and viewing light. The original Adobe RGB photograph needs one intended printer-profile conversion; an already converted device-RGB version must receive no second conversion. Do not apply fitting-target opening instructions to the original photograph. JPEG quantisation and clipping can also produce visible steps; use synthetic high-precision gradients alongside it. Download from Keith Cooper’s page; the image is not distributed in the InkProf repository.
links: Keith Cooper — Printer Test Images, Northlight Images

title: Manual points and an inner shell
lead: Refinement tools is the shared entry point. Choose Manual gamut points / inner shell. The current profile and C1 checks must be complete.
sections: 1. Choose a method

Whole inner gamut shell defaults to the entire surface. Selected inner shell areas restricts it to Lab regions around clicked vertices. Selected RGB neighbourhoods adds device-RGB neighbours. Select area enables picking; Rotate view restores rotation.
2. Set thickness and budget

Shell thickness is ΔE76: shortest geometric Lab distance inward from the surface. Default 3, maximum 50. Near-surface lines may guide thickness; there is no automatic detection. Minimum spacing uses RGB percentage points; Maximum new patches is an upper limit.
3. Review the visual check

Review patches / create TIFF16 shows proposed points against the 3D gamut and their depth against shell thickness. Uncheck unwanted patches. These are ICC predictions, not measured print errors. Selection prioritises gaps in modelled colour coverage.
4. Create and copy TIFF16

Review paper dimensions and choose Create TIFF16 target. Status shows phase and elapsed time, including copying and checksum checks. Select another destination or cancel the copy chooser to retain only the project package. Close exits the gamut view.
5. Register the exact print in step 15

After closing, step 15 returns to registration. For already printed sheets: From saved gamut selection, select the correct proposal.json and Use existing print package. Record your reason. The same TI2 and patch order are preserved; pending C2 patches are not added. Create new print package requires a new print.
6. Measure and rebuild

Step 15 must be Complete before step 16 unlocks. Print at 100% without colour conversion and allow drying. Measure the matching TI2 in step 16 and build the next iteration in step 17. Assess it with a fresh independent verification print.
callout: The shell follows the estimated ICC gamut. Extra measurements may improve the model but cannot expand physical printer gamut. ΔE76 is geometric thickness, not ΔE00 or measured print error.

tag: BEFORE STRIP MEASUREMENT | RGB PRINT CHECK
title: Catch incorrect print settings early
lead: InkProf checks the RGB squares on new pages before the long strip measurement starts. A large difference from an approved print can stop an incorrectly configured print after just a few spot readings.
sections: 1. Check settings even with Photoshop presets

A saved Adobe Photoshop preset is not proof that the current print uses the correct settings. Check colour management in Photoshop and the printer driver, media type, resolution and other project conditions before every print. Base targets and already prepared C2/refinement targets must not receive an extra ICC conversion. Follow the target printing instructions.
2. Measure the three controls before the strips

Every TIFF16 page has R, G and B at the upper right. Nominal 8 × 8 mm squares expand by one pixel on every side, with clearance for the caption. Older targets place them below. Calibrate i1 Pro 2 as instructed; measure stationary in M0 on the same backing. Measure each square ONCE: three readings per page. Use the program button, not the instrument button; do not swipe. Confirm the next sheet at Change printed page. All pages are checked.
3. Approve a known-correct print as the reference

The first check needs a print whose paper and colour settings you have independently checked. After the spot readings, select Approve as print reference. InkProf saves the RGB values as the project reference. Without an approved reference, pages are compared with page 1; this cannot detect a shared error on all pages. Changed recorded printer, paper or print conditions require a new reference.
4. Excessive deviation: Remeasure

Above the review threshold, normally 5 ΔE00, the page, colour and deviation are flagged. Select the row and Remeasure page / colour to read that square once again. The previous value remains in history. Restart all RGB checks repeats the sequence. If the deviation persists, check paper and print settings and reprint as needed. Override… requires a written reason; missing readings cannot be bypassed.
Separate from profiling; older pages still work

Control squares do not affect profile fitting. Older targets without declared RGB controls are measured as before and are not rejected for missing squares. Recorded Paper finish, such as Matte, is retained with the check. Compare matte papers with a correct reference for the same paper; a smaller gamut does not itself mean a larger difference from that reference. Paper type and reasoned exceptions may inform future thresholds, but the threshold does not change automatically.

title: From verification target to an approved certificate
lead: A good measurement result is not a saved approval. Verify the current ICC, record your assessment and then export the certificate.
sections: 1. Row 9: choose a target for the current profile

Run row 9. Choose Create new target, then Default or Other file for ColorChecker (a Lab file, not an image), or Generated balanced set for broader control coverage. 12 extra repeats means 12 extra patches. For an already printed ColorChecker, choose Select existing target; see page 59.
2. Print the saved TIFF16 target

Print at 100% size with the recorded paper and settings. Lab references have already been converted through the ICC once. Do not apply another colour conversion in Photoshop or the driver. Check active settings even with presets. Allow the print to dry. Page 57 describes the RGB check before strip measurement.
3. Row 10: measure the correct print and save

Run row 10 and choose Measure for a new measurement. Check the target name and patch count in Confirm measurement target before choosing Measure this target. Save and finish saves the measurement. Saved revisions selects an already saved measurement of the same target. Previous files remain when the C2 selection changes.
4. Rows 11 and 12: compare and review

Run C3. Compare model and print, then Review feedback. Assess measured errors, grays, repeats and out-of-gamut colours. Approve only for the use and requirements supported by the results. Evidence from an older target or profile does not replace verification of the current ICC.
5. Row 13: save your explicit approval

Run Approve for intended use. Enter intended use, quality requirements and accepted limitations in Your assessment. Tick the confirmation that you reviewed the results and checked print settings against the project. Select Approve for stated use. Example: Approved for photographic prints on the stated paper after ColorChecker verification. Measured colour errors and stated limitations are accepted for this use. Adapt the text to your actual assessment.
6. Row 14: export the certificate

Run Save ICC and measurement certificate. The certificate includes current results and your approval tied to the profile. ColorChecker has its own section with patch names, reference and measured colours, and Delta E00. This is not automatic ISO certification. Two targets are not automatically combined; the current C2 verification provides the evidence.

title: Measure your already printed ColorChecker target
lead: Select a saved verification target for the current ICC without creating or printing it again.
sections: 1. Select the target in step 9

Select C2a. Prepare verification print (TIFF16) and click Run selected step. Choose Select existing target. The list shows saved targets in this project for the current ICC, with names, patch counts and folder IDs.
2. Match the physical print

Choose the ColorChecker entry matching your sheet. Example: Profile test ColorChecker-SG-D50-Lab | 153 patches. The count depends on the reference, repeats and any paper-white controls; not every ColorChecker target has 153 patches. Also compare the folder ID with your print file if several similar targets exist.
3. The saved print package is checked

InkProf checks ICC identity, TI2, manifest and TIFF16 patch values. The same saved print files are reused; no new layout or colour conversion is created. File checks do not prove that the physical print was made with the correct settings.
4. Begin measurement in step 10

Run C2b. Measure verification print / select saved measurement and choose Measure. Confirm measurement target shows the target name and patch count. If they match your sheet, choose Measure this target, then Start measurement. Saved revisions is for measurements that are already saved.
5. Save and approve the result

Complete the measurement and choose Save and finish. Then run steps 11, 12, 13 and 14 for comparison, review, approval and certificate export. Changing the C2 target requires current results and a fresh approval; it does not change the ICC profile.
callout: If you printed both ColorChecker and a broader verification target, select the sheet you will measure first. Targets are measured separately. The certificate uses the current, measured and approved C2 target.

title: Study gradients through the ICC profile
lead: The external delivery folder includes test gradients and a screen preview through the delivered profile.
sections: Open the comparison

Open gradients.html beside the ICC, PDF and HTML certificate. Switch between Original and Soft proof. Select 100 % to inspect without scaling. The ramps include neutral, primary, secondary and blue-sky colours. These are generated test images; this feature does not open a custom JPG.
Which profile is used?

The soft proof uses the exact ICC included in the delivery. The original and preview JPGs contain embedded sRGB. Conversion uses relative colorimetric intent and black point compensation. gradients.json records settings and the profile SHA-256 identity.
Do InkProf profiles work?
A screen preview requires the colour-management engine to use the profile tables for the selected conversion. If it fails, gradients.html states that the preview could not be created.
If the preview is unavailable

A profile may lack support for a colour conversion required by soft proof. The delivery is still saved and gradients.html explains that the preview could not be created. This does not automatically mean the profile is unsuitable for printing.
Save an updated delivery
Save a new external delivery through row 14 or 19. No new measurement is needed solely to add preview assets. Keep the complete folder with evidence.
callout: Soft proof is the profile prediction on screen, not a physical measurement or approval. JPG is 8-bit and may introduce gradient steps itself. Inspect on a calibrated display and retain physical print verification.

tag: TROUBLESHOOTING | PYTHON ON A NEW COMPUTER
title: If a Python package cannot load
lead: InkProf detects failed Python imports and explains how to repair the selected environment. The profiling algorithm does not need to be changed.
sections: Check the installation first

After installation or an update, run setupInkProf(CheckPython=true) in MATLAB. InkProf checks the Python packages needed for analysis and reports by actually importing them. The check also probes required compiled components, such as those in SciPy. An installed package is not necessarily usable.
What does InkProf do when an import fails?

The affected analysis stops before starting. The message identifies the selected Python environment, the original error and commands to repair it. InkProf never reinstalls packages automatically. The standard measurement bridge can run without analysis packages.
Follow the instructions on the affected computer

Copy the repair commands from the message into Terminal on the computer where the failure occurs. They target the Python used by InkProf. Also run pip check as instructed. Do not copy .venv or local-config from another computer.
Check again and continue

Restart MATLAB and run setupInkProf(CheckPython=true). Once the check passes, retry the operation, for example From image in step 15. If it still fails, retain the complete message and Python path for diagnosis.
Version compatibility

An incorrect or incompatible Python or dependency-package version can prevent analysis from working even when the package is installed. InkProf checks the Python version requirement and tests that required packages and their compiled libraries load. Setup also checks that Argyll tools start and report version information. Use the package versions in the requirements files supplied with your InkProf release. The checks test functionality and basic requirements; they do not replace the package versions specified in those files.
callout: This guidance applies to 1.2.1 with current source updates, document revision 2026-10-24. Older release archives may retain older dependencies. Checks and installation do not change saved projects or measurements.

title: Try a higher ICC grid
lead: A denser ICC grid is a separate trial from the same saved measurements. It adds no measured information and requires no new chart.
sections: Start from the shared menu

Refinement tools  >  Try higher ICC grid (same measurements). Choose High or Ultra for B2A or both A2B and B2A, above the original level. Default: B2A: Ultra. Argyll chooses n through quality levels; arbitrary n is not offered.
What changes?

B2A converts to printer RGB. B2A-only retains forward-model and pre-fit quality. Both also changes A2B and pre-fit resolution when pre-smoothing is enabled. Measurements, smoothing value, colourimetry, FWA and mapping follow the original recipe. A separate candidate is saved; the active profile is retained.
Visual numerical verification

Table and bars show actual n and n³ for source and candidate. Select a test gradient for overlaid printer-RGB curves and predicted L*. Dashed: source; solid: candidate. The same nine sRGB paths use relative colorimetric, BPC off and float LittleCMS. grid-curves.json stores values and ICC hashes.
Assess the benefit

Fit, grid and photographic-gradient checks are saved with the candidate. Training error is not independent validation. A denser grid may describe the model in more detail but cannot replace measurements in sparse regions. Use shell printing and measurement to investigate those areas; physical improvement requires print assessment.
callout: Shell refinement changes the measurement set. Grid trials change computed profile tables. Test separately to understand their effects.

title: Next steps and clear delivery
lead: This page explains suggested next rows and how the delivery documents fit together.
sections: Next step
The app suggests the next step from saved, valid results. After step 15, measure in 16, build in 17 and compare in 18. Go to suggested next step selects the step; it does not run it.
Stopped profile build

When numerical checks stop a build, open step 17 results and inspect the latest C1 and Grid reports. Measurements and the previous active ICC are retained. The candidate is not activated automatically. Review the cause before repeating the build.
Optional 3D and measurement groups

During certificate export, choose All measurements, Latest measurements or Certificate only. The 3D viewer separates fitting data from current verification and filters on L*. Latest selects current verification in row 14 and fitting data in row 19. The PDF plot shows only verification colours within L* 40–60. Visible times use the local time zone and offset. Create a new export for revised reports; never overwrite registered export files.

title: First grid: levels and patch budget
sections: Initial levels per axis: what does n³ mean?

For mesh this is the count of equally spaced levels on each of R, G and B. Five levels give 0, 25, 50, 75 and 100 percent: 5³ = 125 combinations. Seven give 343 and nine give 729. These are colours to print and measure, not the ICC internal LUT grid.
Maximum total patches: the complete budget

The cap includes fitting patches, Control patches and Extra repeat patches. The initial values of 575 total, 64 controls and 40 repeats leave 471 fitting places. Extra gray levels add neutral RGB points; levels already in the mesh are not counted twice. Argyll methods do not use Initial levels per axis as an n³ starting grid. Nine initial levels require at least 729 fitting places before extras, so they cannot fit a total budget of 575.See page 49 for larger profiling budgets.
Control patches and Extra repeat patches

Controls are separate from fitting data and provide control/development evidence. Repeats are additional measurements of selected fitting colours and help assess repeatability. Neither setting means the three large R/G/B squares checked before strip measurement.
Preview initial grid and refinement

The mesh preview shows the starting grid and RGB distances. Geometric refinement then fills sparsely covered areas within the budget. Distances are in RGB, not measured ΔE00. Choose a budget appropriate to measurement time and paper layout, and inspect the actual generated count before saving.

title: First-target methods: mesh and Argyll
sections: InkProf mesh refinement

Starts with a regular RGB grid and fills geometric gaps in device RGB. You control levels, budget and placement. No preconditioning ICC is used. Useful for explicit RGB coverage; geometric uniformity does not mean equal Lab colour differences.
Argyll OFPS (default, adaptive)
Optimises point spread; a preconditioning ICC can guide adaptation. A natural Argyll choice for a broad initial target.
Argyll incremental far point
Adds points successively far from existing points. A different spreading procedure from OFPS.
Argyll quasi-random, device space
Uses a low-discrepancy distribution in RGB, seeking space coverage without a regular n³ grid.
Argyll quasi-random, perceptual space
Uses that distribution with perceptual placement. A relevant preconditioning ICC provides a more useful distance basis.
What does default mean?
OFPS is Argyll’s default, but InkProf’s design window normally starts with mesh. Active matte shadow emphasis selects OFPS and locks the method. No method is universally best for every print system.

title: First-target methods: remaining choices
sections: Argyll body-centred cubic, device space
Uses a structured cubic pattern in RGB, with points between the grid corners.
Argyll body-centred cubic, perceptual space
Uses corresponding structured distribution with perceptual placement based on colour response.
Argyll random, device space
Uses random placement in RGB. A small target can contain local clusters and gaps.
Argyll random, perceptual space
Uses random placement in perceptual space, rather than directly in RGB.
Pre-conditioning ICC and Optimized points (-G)

Choose a suitable profile for the same or a similar print system when available. It guides placement; it does not convert the base target or replace new measurements. OFPS and perceptual methods use it when supplied. -G requests more optimised OFPS placement and may take longer; it does not automatically improve every method.
How should I choose?

Use mesh to control an explicit RGB starting grid and geometric gaps. Use OFPS for broad Argyll placement, preferably with a relevant profile. Quasi-random offers another spread; BCC adds structure. Random is mainly an alternative for comparison. Assess reliable measured results rather than choosing by the method name.

title: Mesh: placement and stopping conditions
sections: Centroids (default)
Chooses tetrahedron centroids between existing RGB points. The candidate is inside its tetrahedron. The simplest starting choice.
Sphere centers in tetrahedra
Allows circumsphere centres when they lie inside their tetrahedron. Centroids are also retained as candidates. This seeks gaps without using sphere centres outside the tetrahedron.
All interior sphere centers
Allows centres outside their own tetrahedron if they lie inside the RGB cube. Produces different candidates and coverage. Interior refers to the RGB cube, not a Lab gamut shell.
Max interior gap (0 = off)

A geometric distance condition in normalised RGB, with channels from 0 to 1. Refinement can stop once the largest candidate distance reaches the limit. Zero disables this condition. It is not a ΔE threshold.
Initial gap ratio (0 = off)

Looks for a jump between sorted initial distances and can use it as a stopping level. A value greater than 1 is needed to enable the comparison. Zero disables it. Both gap settings apply to mesh, not Argyll’s spread algorithms.
Check before printing

Inspect placement, actual count and the reason refinement stopped. Preserve the matching TI2 and patch order of a saved TIFF. Distinguish initial geometric mesh from later error-guided Jacobian refinement and shell refinement.

title: Jacobian: why it matters
sections: A local description of model sensitivity

The Jacobian is a 3 × 3 matrix describing how the profile’s predicted L*, a* and b* change when R, G or B changes slightly. Columns represent RGB channels; rows represent Lab components. It distinguishes sensitive directions from directions where RGB changes produce little Lab response.
A simple worked example

Suppose the R column is [0.20; 0.60; -0.10]. Increasing R by one percentage point with G/B unchanged estimates +0.20 L*, +0.60 a* and -0.10 b*. Two percentage points give roughly twice that change, only while the local linear approximation holds. These are teaching values, not measured printer data.
How InkProf computes it

Current code probes the profile forward transform near the RGB point, normally at ±0.5 percentage points per channel. At 0 or 100 percent the probe is restricted to the permitted range. The predicted Lab difference is divided by the actual RGB difference.
Reading the measures

Units are Lab units per RGB percentage point. The norm of predicted local Lab change is geometric sensitivity, not ΔE00. Singular values describe strong and weak directions. A high condition number indicates uneven sensitivity; nearSingular records an almost lost direction.
Model and physical measurement

The matrix comes from the ICC model and inherits its limitations. C3 measurements establish whether the model differs from the print. A high condition number is diagnostic, not by itself a stopping rule or proof of a faulty printer.

title: Jacobian: use and review
sections: What the algorithm actually does

Current InkProf (Jacobian sampling) uses local measured-versus-predicted Lab discrepancies. Candidates are formed between relevant RGB observations and nearby fitting points. The Jacobian estimates the Lab effect of candidate displacement and boosts the priority score with a bounded sensitivity factor.
Why corroboration matters

The algorithm reviews repeats and seeks support from nearby discrepant observations. An isolated error may be flagged for review rather than producing new points. Candidates are quantised to RGB16; already measured RGB values and insufficient spacing are excluded. The patch budget limits selection.
Using the choice

First review C3 and feedback: target identity, colour management, measurement conditions and repeatability. Choose From verification errors and Current InkProf (Jacobian sampling) for a recurring local model discrepancy. Print the proposal unchanged, measure in 16, build in 17 and compare in 18.
What it does not do

The current algorithm does not invert the matrix to correct a patch directly. It does not independently build an ICC or guarantee error reduction. Condition numbers are diagnostic; selection mainly uses predicted local Lab change. More sampling cannot make colours outside the print system’s capability attainable.
Argyll and shell are different choices

Argyll only lets targen place additional RGB points with the current profile. Jacobian refinement combines local measured errors with model sensitivity. Shell refinement seeks coverage gaps near the gamut surface and may be useful without the same C3 error guidance. All three routes use Argyll colprof.
After the next iteration

Compare errors, development evidence, gradients and the earlier profile on equivalent terms. Better priority scores or lower training error do not establish improved print accuracy. Fresh physical verification is needed to assess the new ICC.

title: Enable OBA/FWA after measurement
tag: B2 / B3 / REBUILD FROM SAVED SPECTRA
lead: No code change is needed. The setting already exists; the profile must be rebuilt.
sections: 1. Check the measurement data

Native spectral measurements are required; stored XYZ alone is insufficient. OBA/FWA refers to optical brighteners. The setting enables compensation for their effect, not a new instrument measurement condition.
2. Change the setting

Open Project details and select Compensate optical brighteners (D50). Under Profiling, set Colour data to Spectra (D50 / 2 degrees). Alternatively use B2 > FWA / OBA > Compensate to D50 (also updates Project details). Save the dialog.
3. Rebuild
Save a new B2 recipe in row 6, build B3 in row 7, then run Fit, Grid and C1 in row 8. Manual uses the saved B2 recipe; Automatic creates its own recipes with the project’s FWA choice.
What remains available

Original spectral readings and the frozen B1 input are retained. Changing only the FWA choice normally does not require measuring the base target again. Earlier recipes, profiles and subsequent assessments become out of date. Earlier physical verification does not approve the new profile.
Paper white and verification

If usable paper-white data are missing, B2 offers blank-paper measurement, a saved approved white reference or Cancel. For physical verification of the new profile, perform a fresh C2 print, measurement, C3, feedback and approval in rows 9-14. Row 19 explicitly records the absence of separate print verification.
Limitation

Compensation simulates D50 from M0 spectra; it does not turn M0 into native M1 measurement or prove improved reproduction. Changed materials or printing conditions are a separate issue from changing compensation alone.

title: Save and resume a partial measurement
lead: For large targets, save completed physical rows and continue later.
sections: Save before stopping

Select Save completed rows / pause. Wait for Completed rows saved - measurement paused before closing. Open results folder locates the session. A save requested during a scan waits for the instrument’s row prompt and excludes the row in flight from the checkpoint.
Whole rows only

Partial rows are excluded. With forward/reverse averaging, both scans are required for a completed physical row. A row with only one scan is omitted from the resume snapshot and measured again in both directions.
Open the saved session

Open the measurement routine for the same target. Choose Resume saved session… and the folder containing measurement-checkpoint.json. The dialog states the completed-row count, page, printed row and direction at which measurement resumes.
Confirm and continue

Choose Resume measurement and confirm Resume same printed sheets. Use exactly the same physical sheets. If you printed again or replaced a page, choose Cancel and start a new session with fresh RGB checks. The checksum identifies chart data, not physical paper.
Follow instrument instructions

Calibrate when prompted and wait for the displayed row instruction before scanning. Saved scan settings and RGB controls are reused. Restart the first unfinished row from its beginning; for paired measurements scan forward, then reverse.
Finish and review

After all rows, select Save and finish and review the measurement as usual. A checkpoint does not complete the workflow step. An unexpected interruption may lose scans since the last checkpoint. Changed chart data, settings or saved readings are rejected.
callout: Included in v1.2.2: automatically tested; real-instrument resume validation remains necessary.

title: Remeasurement and RGB controls
sections: Continue after rereading

When navigating back within an active measurement and rereading successfully, InkProf selects the following scan pass. For paired measurements follow the forward/reverse instructions for the same physical row. Separate remeasurement of a previously saved row creates a revision that must be reviewed and accepted.
Reuse only for the same print

A new session’s RGB dialog can offer Reuse checks for same print. Select the earlier session folder with approved RGB checks. Target and control-definition identities are checked. Do not reuse for reprinted or replaced pages, even when chart data are identical.
Check every page

For a new print, measure R, G and B on every page. These controls are separate from profiling patches and excluded from fitting. Approved controls are retained when resuming the same saved partial measurement.
Larger squares in newly generated targets

RGB squares gain 0.5 mm on each edge: 1 mm in nominal width and height. The existing one-pixel raster extension on each edge remains. Measurement rectangles and labels follow the geometry. Existing TIFF files are unchanged; generate a new target to use the larger squares.
If RGB checking is interrupted
A cancelled or failed RGB check no longer permanently disables startup. Correct the problem and start again. This does not automatically approve measurements or exceptions.
callout: Included in v1.2.2. Restart InkProf to load the updated code. Existing print files are unchanged.

title: Transfer measurements to i1Profiler
lead: An existing InkProf measurement can be transferred as CGATS text and used to build a profile in i1Profiler without a new print or measurement.
sections: Save CGATS from the app

When saving the ICC and certificate in step 14 or 19, tick Include CGATS for i1Profiler when saving ICC/certificate in the main window. No additional CGATS dialog is shown. The delivery includes i1profiler-measurement.txt and its provenance JSON. This exports the selected original profiling measurement, not accumulated refinement data or C2 verification. The option is not shown for imported profiles without a profiling measurement. Only complete native M0 measurements with XRGA and 36 spectral bands are supported.
Use the correct workflow

In i1Profiler choose Printer, RGB Printer, then Profiling. Open Measurement, Load and select CGATS as the file type. Load the .txt file. Do not rename it to .mxf: changing the extension does not change the format and causes a CxF read error.
What the test verified

On macOS with i1Profiler 3.8.5, the user imported the Canon measurement of 2,200 patches and created an ICC profile. Inspection of its embedded CxF data found all 2,200 target and measurement objects; all 36 spectral values per patch matched the source within numerical precision. Chart 2033 Patches was a retained name, not the transferred patch count.
Precision and page layout

The exporter retains RGB precision, but i1Profiler rounded RGB to integers on the 0–255 scale in the inspected embedded data. The largest difference was about one RGB step. The import view showed one page; embedded location data listed four. Do not use the display layout to remeasure the original print.
Scope and limitations

The routine supports complete native M0 measurements, XRGA and 36 bands from 380 to 730 nm. Here M0 was inferred from the instrument workflow, not explicitly reported in TI3. No FWA compensation is applied during export. The accompanying JSON records checksums and provenance. Import and profile creation were tested for this case; print quality and other versions remain unverified.
callout: The original measurement and InkProf profile are unchanged. Preserve JSON/TI3 as the full-precision source.

title: Identify the printed target before measuring
lead: A saved date alone is not enough. Match the target type, page count and original package path to the physical sheet.
images: Synthetic interface example: no real measurement or instrument session was started.
sections: Base target or C2 verification?

Step 3. Measure / select measurement revision reads the base target saved in step 2. A C2 print belongs to C2b. Measure verification print / select saved measurement. If its package is already selected, go directly to that measurement step; do not generate the target again. After all rows are read, choose Save and finish, then C3. Compare model and print and Review feedback.
Target locked is intentional

A prepared measurement is bound to its TI2. The disabled Choose chart button now says Target locked. To change the target, close the measurement window and select the matching target in the workflow. Do not substitute a similar-looking chart while a session is prepared or partially measured.
What the window shows

The summary shows patch count, target type when recorded, page count, saved local time and UTC. Target details shows the full path and offers a page preview. Missing historical metadata is not guessed. Compare these facts with the printed footer. Package creation time does not prove the physical print date or drying time.

title: Readable print folders and traceability
lead: Copy TIFF16 for printing creates a separate delivery with the project name instead of a UUID-only folder.
sections: Folder naming

Example: My printer paper_iter-1_c2_20261024-123456. The prefix is the saved project name, followed by the workflow cycle at copy, step and local copy timestamp. A collision creates another numbered folder rather than overwriting a previous delivery. This is the project name, not an independently entered ICC/profile description.
PROJECT_INFO.txt

The UTF-8 text file retains the exact project name and ID, original project path, workflow step, current cycle/iteration ID, target-origin cycle/iteration ID when found in history, UTC and local copy/creation times, target description when present, source TI2 and its SHA-256, project printing settings and copied filenames with SHA-256. Unknown origin metadata stays unknown.
Copies versus originals

PRINTING.txt retains printing instructions. print-delivery.json carries the structured receipt; the workflow also records the copy in project reports/history. TIFF data is copied and checked byte for byte. The physical sheet is not identified merely by a hash: match its footer and documented settings. The TIFF-only delivery does not replace the original TI2/layout for measurement.
A target can outlive an iteration

A base or C2 target may have been created in an earlier cycle. The folder names the workflow cycle at copy; PROJECT_INFO.txt separately records the target-origin cycle recovered from matching history. Package creation date and copy date are different events and neither proves when the sheet was physically printed.
Complete target-package copy

The optional complete-package copy from refinement tools uses the same project-based naming and project identification when its source is inside a recognised project. Without project context it uses a generic readable print-copy name; missing project/iteration facts are not invented.

title: Verification feedback and complete delivery
sections: C2a prepares the print and C2b measures it

C2a. Prepare verification print (TIFF16) saves or selects the print package. C2b. Measure verification print / select saved measurement reads that sheet. Choose Measure for a new print, not Resume saved session. Save and finish, then run C3. This verifies the existing ICC; it does not build a new profile.
Read C3 feedback

Run Review feedback to open a readable feedback window. Reopen it with Open selected step results while feedback is selected. C3 files are verification-check.md and verification-check.json under targets/<target>/checks/<check>. Each check has its own folder. Compare reports with the same ICC and target; distinguish error against desired Lab from error against the ICC prediction.
Approval and certificate are separate actions

Selecting a row navigates only. Run Open review and approval, review the results, tick the confirmation and save your assessment. Then select row 14, Save ICC and measurement certificate, and click Save ICC and certificate... Choose Also save copies elsewhere to select the bundle name and location. Save in project only keeps the delivery inside the project. A previous step-19 numerical-only export no longer hides this next step after print approval.
The exact verified ICC is included

The external delivery folder contains <profile>-verified-original.icc, a byte-identical copy of the checked ICC. The normally named ICC has updated name metadata; an optional -v4.4.icc is a converted variant and is not the original verified file. delivery.json records verifiedOriginalICCFile and verifiedOriginalICCSHA256. Keep the whole bundle, including underlag.
Repeat verification after changing printer settings

Print the same target again with the intended settings and document the actual CO/coating choice, media, quality and drying time for each sheet. Start a new C2b measurement; previous measurements remain. Compare the matching C3 reports. A saved Automatic setting alone does not establish which physical CO setting was used.

title: Workflow updates - 25 October 2026
lead: Workflow changes included in release 1.3.0.
sections: Review and lock once

Step 4 keeps the measurement preview open until Continue to assessment. B1 validates the selected revision, opens a modal Lock profile input confirmation, then saves a checked snapshot. Activity and elapsed time are shown during validation and saving. Suggested navigation is B1, B2, B3; B2 is shown for recipe review, while Automatic B3 still creates its own recipes.
Patch counts and result windows

Initial B3 no longer asks for extra refinement patch parameters. Those apply when adding patches or continuing an iteration. C1 saves its numerical reports without opening successive result windows automatically; use Open selected step results. C2a handles verification-target preparation; choose existing files when reusing a printed sheet.
Correct recorded details

When Project details changes, distinguish Correct recorded details from Changed actual setup. A documentation correction requires a reason and unchanged physical conditions. Original file hashes are checked and a new audit record stores before/after values. Numerical processing changes cannot use this exception. Existing stale steps are not automatically restored.
ISSUE-001 closed

ISSUE-001 was closed by user decision on 2026-10-25 after several measurements without observed problems. Remaining uncertainty was accepted for current use. This is not a claim that a full noise-propagation/refitting study was performed; real numerical alerts and independent print verification still apply.

title: Measurement and delivery updates
lead: Workflow changes included in release 1.3.0.
sections: RGB and other spot measurements

RGB controls, single-patch replacements and paper-white spots use a short start sound for screen-triggered and i1 Pro 2 instrument-button measurements. Calibration does not use the spot start sound. RGB colour rows show page, colour and progress only. The temporary sound-test button has been removed. Page changes are shown inline without a separate confirmation window.
Cancel and resume safely

Skip / close and the window close button can cancel the RGB control dialog while calibration is waiting. Saved requests, transcripts and readings remain. Partial output lines no longer block GUI polling, and Argyll debug text after a prompt is handled. Main workflow activity is cleared on interruption. Restart InkProf after source changes; resume saved chart rows only for the same physical print.
Refinement print copies

After successfully saving and registering gamut patches from Refinement tools, the workflow gamut window closes. The standalone viewer also closes after successful TIFF16 creation. To copy an existing refinement target, select row 15 in the main table and use Copy TIFF16 for printing..., then choose Downloads. The new folder identifies the project and iteration and contains printing files and traceability information. The source project is preserved.
Timed certificate delivery

Step 14 shows activity and elapsed time while collecting evidence, rendering figures and PDFs, preparing ICC variants, and copying and verifying delivery files. The external bundle includes the exact checked ICC as <name>-verified-original.icc as well as named delivery variants. A stored certificate is not regenerated in place; create a new export revision when changes are needed.

title: Gamut boundaries and extended targets
sections: Explore the current model boundary

View gamut offers Gamut boundary exploration (both sides), alongside the existing inner-shell and selected-area methods. Set Boundary distance in Delta E76, minimum RGB spacing and maximum NEW patches. Candidates are printable device RGB, not invented out-of-range colours. A negative signed distance means predicted outside the current mesh; it does not prove physical gamut expansion.
Extend latest target

Tick Extend latest target to combine the latest completed gamut print for the exact current ICC with new points. Unprinted proposals are skipped. Previous fitting/development points and supplementary shadow points are retained; exact duplicates and existing training RGB are excluded. Controls are regenerated. Started or paused measurements prevent extending that same target. The earlier TIFF, TI2 and readings remain unchanged.
Print and measure the NEW version

The complete target is saved normally in the project. The optional external-copy dialog defaults to Downloads; Cancel skips only the external copy. Print every page without colour conversion. Step 16 measures the new TI2, and step 17 builds the next profile with the earlier training. Do not measure an earlier layout with the new TI2. View gamut closes after successful creation and the copy dialog; cancellation/error leaves it open.

title: Review measured Lab density
sections: Read the measurements

Refinement tools > Review measured Lab density / balanced trial lists close measured Lab groups and their RGB span. Readings is an integer count of repeated RGB16 observations; maximum Delta E00 describes their repeatability. Similar Lab at different RGB may describe saturation. No original measurement is deleted, overwritten or averaged.
Set, recalculate, select

Adjust Lab distance (Delta E76), Target per group and Repeat review (Delta E00), then Recalculate. Defaults 1 / 4 / 1 are provisional. Use balancing applies automatic representatives to checked groups; unchecked groups keep all rows. Select all checks/highlights all groups; Clear all restores every row to the proposed input. Neutrals, lightness/RGB extrema and inconsistent repeats stay protected. The target count may therefore be exceeded.
Build a separate candidate

Close only closes the review. Build separate balanced candidate uses the reviewed subset and is disabled when zero points would be omitted. Try different settings and Recalculate rather than forcing removal. Both profiles are compared to ALL original fitting observations, including omitted rows, to available reserved development patches and to matching photographic gradients. These are diagnostics, not final independent print verification. No candidate automatically replaces the active profile.

title: Activity, provenance and computer changes
sections: Visible work stages

Density review, Recalculate and the balanced trial show elapsed time and current phase: input verification, original snapshots, ICC build, all-patch comparison, original/candidate gradients, available development checks and result saving. Changing settings requires Recalculate before building. Trial parameters, checked groups, source rows and SHA-256 hashes remain in separate review/trial records.
One environment per program

Each program has its own .venv with Python 3.13.6 and the same pinned requirements. From the code folder use setup_python_environment("check"), "sync" or "rebuild". A rebuild preserves the previous environment as a backup and restores it on failure. Do not commit or move a .venv as a portable replacement for rebuilding it. Projects and measured originals are separate from the runtime.
Native Argyll and documentation scope

The program folder includes separately licensed ArgyllCMS 3.5.0 for ARM and Intel macOS, with upstream notices and provenance. Native tools are preferred and checked for actual startup. This document describes release 1.4.0. Restart the app after source updates.
